newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says security pact helps bid for NATO.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says security pact helps bid for NATO.

text.p: Bulgaria said on Wednesday the NATO-Russia security pact opened the way for partnership in Europe and could improve the Balkan state's prospects of joining NATO.

"This historic accord, which formally ends the era of confrontation in Europe and clears the way for the alliance to expand eastwards, gives us grounds to reaffirm Bulgaria's strong desire to join NATO," Foreign Ministry spokesman Radko Vlaikov told a news conference.
On Tuesday NATO leaders and Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed the Founding Act on Mutual Relations designed to bind Russia into a new European security order.
"We praise the Russia-NATO accord which ends an era of confrontation in Europe and reaffirms the rignt of each country to decide how to guarantee its security," said Vlaikov.
In February Bulgaria's caretaker government adopted a declaration stating a desire for full NATO membership.
Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces, which won the April election and formed a cabinet last week, has set NATO membership as a foreign policy priority.

NATO is expected to issue the first invitations to prospective new members at a summit in Madrid in July and Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are considered the most likely candidates to join in the first wave of enlargement.
